content:
Kai M: starting canary for Mariner-31B (int8) — noticing rare OOMs and high tail latency on multi-k turn jobs. repro with mixed traffic (long single requests + medium batches).
Zoe H: single-request or batch-induced? any kernel traces?
Kai M: usually a single 1.5k token request + concurrent batch_size=3. GPU free memory fragmented into many small slabs. attaching a quick alloc trace below.
Rahul P: did onboarding use prefetch/warmup and a high reserve_fraction?
Kai M: yes onboarding template set prefetch=true and reserve_fraction=0.58. I ran a smoke disabling prefetch and saw lower fragmentation.
Zoe H: can you paste the runtime patch you tested?
Kai M: patch I iterated on locally: ```
model: mariner-31b-int8
batching:
  max_batch_size: 4
  preferred_batch_size: [1,2]
  batch_timeout_ms: 10
prefetch:
  enabled: false  # try hybrid later
kv_cache:
  reserve_fraction: 0.45
  slot_compactor: {enabled: true, sweep_interval_sec: 600}
router:
  heuristics:
    - name: long-gen-no-prefetch
      if: request.max_new_tokens >= 700
      route: pool=no-prefetch
generation:
  default_max_new_tokens: 512
  max_seq_len: 8192
```
Rahul P: lowering reserve_fraction and turning off prefetch helped in your smoke runs? numbers?
Kai M: before: ~8% OOMs in 100 long-gen traces. after: 0 OOMs, frag_ratio median rose from 0.28 -> 0.6, token throughput ~+2% reduction only.
eval-bot: mariner-31b-int8 eval: BLEU delta -0.4%, QA F1 -0.9% vs float32. within thresholds for canary.
Zoe H: quality ok. plan: keep config for canary, add a transient adaptive throttle: if active_frag_ratio < 0.35 then temporarily cap effective_max_new_tokens = min(requested, 512) for 5m per pod.
Rahul P: good idea. also add metric frag_ratio = largest_free_block / total_free_mem and alert when <0.33 for 10m. ops-bot, can you create that?
ops-bot: created metric mariner_frag_ratio and alert rule frag_ratio_low -> notify #pager if <0.33 for 10m.
Kai M: I'll push branch canary/mariner-int8-fragfix with these changes + a feature flag for a more aggressive allocator behavior (eager_free_temp). gated to dev only.
Zoe H: also propose router fallback to int4 variant for very long generations if int8 can't satisfy memory on the fly — might be counterintuitive but int4 smaller memory footprint. need eval for int4 quality.
Rahul P: we should be cautious: int4 quality regressions may be larger. schedule a quick eval on representative long-gen prompts.
eval-bot: scheduled eval: mariner-31b-int4 vs int8 on long-gen prompt set (200 examples) — will post results in 2h.
Kai M: infra-bot: canary rollout started 2/4 pods. smoke job queued (100 long-gen requests interleaved with batch traffic).
infra-bot: smoke-run result: 100 long-gen runs -> 1 OOM (transient), 99 success. old config had 7 OOMs for same test set.
Zoe H: looks promising. follow-ups: 1) run 24h canary with real traffic 2) add nightly low-QPS long-gen compactor exercise job 3) add dashboard panel: frag_ratio, free_chunks, compactor_runs per pod.
Rahul P: and we need rollback criteria: if >2 OOMs/hr OR frag_ratio alert fires >3 times in 1h, revert to previous config.
Kai M: added checklist and rollback criteria in PR. tagging @oncall. will post 12h metrics here. :thumbsup:
eval-bot: mariner-int4 quick eval done: on long-gen set BLEU delta vs int8 -1.6%, coherence drops on ~12% of examples. recommend not automatic fallback to int4 without tenant opt-in.
Zoe H: good catch. keep int4 fallback as a manual option for tenants who accept quality tradeoff. we stick to throttle + router no-prefetch route for now.
Kai M: logs (snippet): ```
[2026-04-05T09:12:10Z] alloc failed requested=1.4GiB free_chunks=210 largest_free=320MiB total_free=1.1GiB
[2026-04-05T09:12:10Z] OOM during kv_alloc slot=21 seq=1536
[2026-04-05T09:12:12Z] compactor: fast-pass migrated 10 entries reclaimed=640MiB
```
Rahul P: that trace shows compactor rescue working but we prefer to avoid triggers. good plan.
infra-bot: alert created: mariner_frag_ratio_low -> paging eng-ml if persists for 10m.
Kai M: thanks team. will post 12h and 24h canary metrics in this thread. reopen if we see regressions.
